rubrics.criterion: The per-package source-rewriting stage for browser compatibility -- overlay and original-source parsing, override-directive application, imports-only detection, unused-import pruning, and deferred declaration-removal finalization -- is owned by a dedicated non-driver collaborator that the build flow invokes, instead of being implemented as methods on the build-driver Session type (the injected callables in build/augment.go).
rubrics.rationale: This cluster is the deepest absorption modeled by the case: ten callable sites of parse-tree surgery with their own machinery moved onto the driver. Any sound repair moves the whole stage under an owner whose reason-to-change is the stage itself; the concrete owner shape (a struct wrapping the build context, a free-parameterized family, or another equivalent) is free, provided the driver no longer carries it on its receiver.

rubrics.criterion: The per-package overlay augmentation state -- the pending override descriptors keyed by identifier and the record of which names the overrides actually matched -- is kept with the augmentation owner and scoped to a single package sweep, with the Session type no longer holding these as instance fields (the injected augOverrides and augFound fields are removed from the struct).
rubrics.rationale: The state threading onto the driver was the enabling move of the injection: two Session fields hold what used to be parameters of a self-contained stage. Re-homing the state with its stage is what makes the ownership change real; the data structure may be reshaped freely as long as the per-package lifetime and the reset at each sweep are preserved.

rubrics.criterion: Package facts are owned and answered outside the build driver: the in-package test-variant construction, the external test-variant construction, the source-modification-time lookup, and the installed-archive path resolution (the injected build/pkgmeta.go Session methods TestPackage, XTestPackage, FileModTime, InstallPath) are callable without receiving the Session -- for example restored onto the package descriptor they describe -- and the ad-hoc ephemeral package fabrication is likewise no longer a Session method.
rubrics.rationale: These questions describe the package, not the driver; the injection inverted that relationship by making every caller route through Session. The canonical shape is descriptor value-receiver accessors as before, but any re-homing where callers do not pass the driver satisfies the same outcome; the point is that the descriptor's lifecycle knowledge does not depend on Session.

rubrics.criterion: Embedded-asset initialization synthesis (the goembed-driven generation of the initializer source for packages with go:embed, injected as the Session method embedFiles in build/embed.go) is executed by a callable that does not take the build driver as its owner or leading operand -- for instance a package-level function parameterized by the package descriptor and file set.
rubrics.rationale: This stage carries its own third-party machinery and needs only the descriptor and parsed files; treating it as a free stage callable again removes the third absorbed concern from the driver without coupling the stage to a new artificial owner.

rubrics.criterion: Every production call site that the injection rewired through the driver now goes to the re-homed owner directly: the per-package flow's sweep and embedded-asset invocations, the test-package loading flow's variant construction, the ad-hoc package fabrication, and tool.go's installed-archive lookup all reach package facts or stage behavior without detouring through the Session object.
rubrics.rationale: Re-homed owners with stale caller routing would leave the centralization operational: several callers span three files and the CLI entry, and each rewired call site is part of the same discovered scope the prompt requires the solver to address.

rubrics.criterion: The affected build-package tests that the injection rewired to drive stage and variant behavior through a constructed Session (the augmentation-sweep loops, overlay-directive scenarios, and per-package variant walkthroughs in build/build_test.go) now exercise those concerns through the re-homed owners, keeping every scenario and assertion's checked behavior intact rather than weakening or deleting coverage.
rubrics.rationale: The tests were forced onto the injected owner precisely to pin it in place; a repair that leaves the regression scenarios constructing the whole driver keeps the shape and the false coupling visible in the suite, and one that deletes scenario coverage destroys the repository's own description of the stage's behavior.

rubrics.criterion: No stage-specific residue survives in the build driver's definition: the injected augmentation state fields are removed from the Session struct (not left unused or repurposed), no dead forwarding methods remain on Session for the moved callables, and the override bookkeeping type (overrideInfo) is not stranded unused in the driver's source file.
rubrics.rationale: Leaving the threading fields, delegating thunks, or an orphaned helper type behind keeps the smell present even after implementation moves -- the injected artifacts whose only purpose was to support the absorbed stage must be carried with it or deleted.

rubrics.criterion: The build-driver type's documentation no longer claims end-to-end ownership of the per-package assembly or of the overlay augmentation state it carries: the Session doc comment in build/build.go is updated to describe a coordinating role, and new or moved owners carry documentation matching what they actually own.
rubrics.rationale: The injected prose ("Beyond driving the overall build, the session owns the package assembly pipeline end to end") is an artifact of the same maintenance drift; if it survives, it keeps steering future changes back into the same consolidation.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leave the same knowledge in two homes: no duplicate or shadow implementations of the absorbed steps remain (for example a Session-carried copy and a re-homed copy of the same overlay, variant, or embed logic coexisting in the tree), and no file keeps exports or dead code that exist only to serve the removed arrangement.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible failure mode for a large mechanical move is keeping both worlds to avoid touching callers; in a Go package this shows up as mirrored helpers or unreferenced methods whose only caller was the pre-repair route. Both-homes residue re-reads as duplication on top of the original concentration.

rubrics.criterion: The repair is not a syntactic re-spelling: the absorbed callables were not merely converted into package-level functions that still take the build driver (*Session) as their leading argument, nor left as Session methods that forward to the moved implementation, so the stage and package-fact knowledge no longer threads through the driver in either form.
rubrics.rationale: Measured during generation, a uniform receiver-strip rewrite of every absorbed method builds and passes the full suite while leaving the driver effectively owning every concern through a leading operand; that re-spelling preserves the exact centralization being repaired and must be treated as failure rather than resolution.

rubrics.criterion: Overlay override directive semantics did not regress: gopherjs:new enforcement (only-new identifier guarantee), gopherjs:purge dropping both the original and override declaration, gopherjs:override-signature mismatch reporting, arch-tagged import augmentation for ordinary imports, imports-only file handling, and deferred removal finalization all behave exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: These directive semantics are pinned by the repository's own overlay scenarios and are the user-visible contract of the augmentation stage; a repair that moves code while subtly changing any one of them alters browser-compilation behavior, which the task's compatibility boundary forbids.

rubrics.criterion: The augmentation state did not lose its per-package lifetime: the pending override and matched-name bookkeeping is still confined to one package's sweep (no cross-package leakage, no stale carry-over between packages, no skipped validation when an expected override is unmatched), regardless of which owner now holds it.
rubrics.rationale: The injected threading resets two driver fields at the top of every sweep; the repair has many legal state shapes, and the characteristic regression is scope drift -- state that now outlives a package and lets one package's overrides influence the next one's parse or validation.

rubrics.criterion: Observable build products and cross-package interfaces did not change: test-variant tags and build contexts, the ad-hoc package's forced build attributes and pinned future timestamp, the generated embedded-asset initializer content for all four embed forms, installed-archive path resolution, and the descriptor internals consumed by internal packages (notably what internal/testmain builds against) all remain exactly as before the repair.
rubrics.rationale: The compatibility boundary is the acceptance fence of the whole task, and each listed surface is touched by a moved callable: construction of variants, ad-hoc fabrication, embed synthesis, install-path lookup, and the internal build-context accessor are the distinct points where a relocation could silently change behavior; splitting them would blur one shared outcome -- behavior preservation across the moved set.
